title: Feelings & Emotion-Coaching Space
strapline: A space and a way of being with children where every feeling is named, welcomed and worked through together.
intent: Children learn that all feelings are allowed — it's what we do with them that we work on together.
Children build a rich emotional vocabulary, moving beyond happy and sad to frustrated, nervous, jealous, proud.
Children experience an adult who names and validates their feeling before problem-solving — co-regulation modelled again and again.
Children develop empathy, reading feelings in faces, stories and friends and responding with care.
Children take the first steps from adult-supported to self-directed emotional regulation.
implementation: Live the four steps of emotion coaching: notice the feeling, name it and empathise, set limits if needed, then problem-solve together.
Lead with connection: 'you're really cross the tower fell — that is so frustrating' before any 'what could we try?'.
Stock the space with feelings faces, emotion cards, mirrors, and picture books that put words to the whole range of emotions.
Name your own feelings out loud, appropriately — 'I felt nervous before the fire drill' — so children see adults have and handle feelings.
Catch and label the small everyday feelings all day, not just the big blow-ups, so the vocabulary grows in calm moments.
Keep limits kind and firm — 'I won't let you hit; you can stamp your feet or squeeze this' — feelings welcomed, unsafe actions not.
key_questions: What are you feeling right now?
What happened that made you feel that way?
How do you think your friend is feeling?
What could we do that might help?
Have you ever felt like the character in this story?

impact.text: Children name basic feelings in themselves and in pictures and stories.
Children talk about feelings, what caused them, and what helps them feel better.
Children show genuine empathy — noticing and comforting a sad or hurt friend unprompted.
Children regulate big feelings using strategies that work for them, with adults nearby not in charge.
Children express emotions clearly and are soothed through warm co-regulation.

enhancements: An emotions display with children's own photos pulling different faces, that they helped make.
A feelings check-in routine at the start of the day and after lunch.
A basket of feelings stories rotated with the emotions the group is working through.
Small-world and puppet play scenarios that let children rehearse feelings and resolutions.
A 'kindness caught' moment each day, noticing when a child comforted or helped another.

playing_exploring: Children explore feelings safely through stories, puppets, mirrors and small-world play.
Pulling faces and matching emotion cards makes naming feelings playful.
active_learning: Feeling genuinely understood helps children calm and re-engage with confidence.
Children keep trying strategies for big feelings, supported not rescued.
creating_thinking: Children link cause and feeling — this happened, so I feel that — and generate solutions.
They take another's perspective, imagining how a friend might feel.
